title: Longhair's club circuit and the ism
summary: Longhair played the Pepper Pot and the Greystone, wiggled his foot for the ism, and had Afro-Caribbean feeling.

bands.name: Professor Longhair and the Shuffling Hungarians

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: So when, it seems like at some point, you know, let's get back to Professor Longhair. I wanted to ask you some more questions.
What kind of, when you joined his band, was that, was that like top?

Oh, yeah. Because Professor Longhair played the Pepper Potty. He played the Greystone. We went out to Back Vashery, Front Vashery. We went to Baton Rouge. You know, all these little places along the river had little nightclubs. And Professor Longhair was popular about playing these places. And we went to these places. And we played on weekends. Mostly weekends, it was. And his main spot was, like I said, the hi-hat. He played the hi-hat all the time. Or down at Charlie Armstead's. Club Desire, yeah. And we used to, the people, when we went on the gig with a fest, the people would take and put a pillar at the bottom of their piano, you know. Because down at the bottom of his piano, his brother was an upright piano, you know. And he had a panel down there. Right. Yeah. You know. And Professor Longhair, when he played, he wiggled his right foot. Uh-huh. You understand? And I was, he called that the ism.
Yeah. If you didn't have that ism, you couldn't be in Professor Longhair as bad.

I hope I did. Yeah. I learned a lot from Fest, man. I learned a lot of music that people who are trying to play it today, that feeling, you know. His feeling of music had African Jamaican rhythms to it. Yeah. And reggae, too. And in those days, reggae was not even recognized in our culture of music, but it's there. Uh-huh. It's there, you know. Yeah. I'm not getting off the subject. Well, in 1988, when we took a tour of Africa and visited Gore Island off of Dakar from Senegal, you understand? Uh-huh. We went to the slave house that the last Spanish slave house had sent slaves out to three different parts of the United States. And this is where our origin must come from. Uh-huh. Some landed in Jamaica. Some went to North Carolina. And the rest came to Louisiana. Uh-huh. We've got that, uh-huh. We've got that feeling installed. And so, and Professor Longhair always played like that. You know? He called, one time, the name of the band was Professor Longhair and the Shuffling Hungarians. But he didn't know what Hungarians were. You know?
